newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian state leader says strikes cost millions.
newsitem.headline: Australian state leader says strikes cost millions.

text.p: The cost to industry of the ongoing industrial campaign against proposed changes to Western Australia's industrial relations laws "would run into the hundreds of millions of dollars", state Premier Richard Court said on Tuesday.

"When (you consider) that industry has had virtually a week without power and then you've got these rolling stoppages, whether it is with shipping or the construction industry or whatever, it is causing damage," Court said during a media conference.
His news conference coincided with a 24-hour strike by waterside workers at the Port of Fremantle which left five ships, including two tankers and a container vessel, stranded.
A Port Authority spokesman said such a would usually cost owners of tanker ships about A$70,000 and container vessels about A$50,000.

In related industrial action, thousands of metal workers began a 24-hour strike at midnight Monday. Dairy production workers were also on strike on Tuesday for 24 hours and later this week public hospitals are expected to be affected by industrial action by cleaners, caterers and orderlies.

Public sector employees will attend a lunchtime stopwork meeting on Thursday to protest against the legislation, which includes provisions for compulsory pre-strike secret ballots and limitations on political donations.
